Eval walks cheapest-first, first hit wins - keep_on_error status compare, span-latency timestamp math, the baggage pair, then the OTTL tail - and the whole built-in prefix is guaranteed alloc-free; BAGGAGE rides span attributes under configurable keys (t0_attribute/elapsed_ms_attribute, defaults baggage.t0/baggage.elapsed_ms, epoch millis), values accepted as int64 OR decimal-digit string because baggage is a string on the wire (a generic baggage->attribute copier yields strings, custom stampers write ints, and refusing either half refuses half the deployments), parsed by a hand-rolled digit loop since strconv's error path allocates; MISSING baggage is a propagation gap that simply cannot fire the condition (ADR-003 r5) while MALFORMED-but-present is counted separately - a wrong-typed value is an upstream bug and an absent one an un-instrumented hop, so one number would hide whichever is rarer; a positive sub-millisecond threshold FLOORS to 1ms instead of truncating to 0, because truncation turns a configured+documented+exported condition into a dead one; BASELINE is the trace id's trailing 56 bits (the OTel consistent-probability randomness source, random under W3C trace-context level 2) compared against round(rate*2^56) precomputed at Build - no hash and no float on the hot path, identical on every instance by construction, never published; the [0,1]-with-NaN-rejection bound in Config.Validate is a CORRECTNESS bound and not input hygiene, because each way out of range fails differently: rate>1 keeps everything (defined, useless), rate>=256 hits an implementation-defined float64->uint64 conversion that DIVERGES BY ARCHITECTURE so a mixed fleet would compute different baselines from one config and destroy the identical-verdict property the design rests on, and rate<0 or NaN is silently swallowed by Build's positive-rate gate (NaN compares false against everything) leaving the baseline off; POLICIES are a named {name,condition} list, one ottlspan condition each, OR-composed first-match-wins, names unique and non-empty since they key telemetry attribution and the per-chain bench baselines, PARSE-TWICE (Validate against throwaway nop settings so a typo fails config load loudly, Build with the component's real settings - parsing is the only way to validate OTTL and no real TelemetrySettings exists during Validate); eval errors are IGNORE-AND-COUNT with warn-once per policy and there is deliberately NO error_mode field (ADR-005 r2): propagating fails the batch, and a receiver retrying a poison span turns one malformed record into an endlessly retried batch;
